record.paper_title: Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund inequalities and the Numerical approximation of singular integrals for exponential weights: Methods, Results and Open Problems, Some new, some old.
record.context_brief: Convergence criteria for product integration rules
record.original_question: Let I=(c,d) with -infinity <= c < 0 < d <= infinity, and let w:I -> (0,infinity) be an admissible exponential weight satisfying the regularity, endpoint-growth, T-function comparability, and local Lipschitz-type conditions in the admissibility definition: Q=log(1/w), Q(0)=0, Q' is nondecreasing, Q tends to infinity at both endpoints, T(x)=xQ'(x)/Q(x) is one-sided quasi-monotone and bounded below by a constant greater than 1, T(y) is locally comparable to T(y(1 - epsilon_0/T(y))), and Q' satisfies the stated local integral smoothness bound. Let f be a smooth function such that f w decays at specified endpoint rates, and let k be a specified kernel that typically decays near the endpoints. For the scalar integral I[k,f]=integral_I f(t)k(t) dt, and also for the weighted Hilbert-transform case I[k,f](x)=principal value integral_I (f(t)w(t))/(x-t) dt, define product-integration rules from a node array chi_n by I_n^*[k,f](x)=sum_{j=1}^n w_{j,n}(x) f(x_{j,n}), with the weights w_{j,n} chosen so that the rule reproduces every algebraic polynomial of degree at most n-1. What necessary and sufficient conditions on the admissible weight, the kernel, the function class, and the node arrays guarantee mean convergence and pointwise convergence of these product-integration rules to the corresponding integral?

artifact.category_tag: Product integration rules for exponential weights
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem on convergence criteria for product integration rules associated with admissible exponential weights. No published necessary-and-sufficient characterization for both mean and pointwise convergence in this general admissible-weight setting appears to have been established; only sufficient conditions for special weight classes (e.g., Freud and Erdős weights) are known.
